rules.statement: Apply build-scroll-3d-product-story to the current car GLB and directly deliver the selected five-shot virtual-FPV narrative as a production WebGL scroll story; no human screening or narrative approval may block implementation.

Document applicable automotive or technical product advertising cases from primary or creator-owned sources, extracting narrative thesis, transferable methods, and limitations for this concept car model.
Develop and compare at least two materially different car-story routes before selecting one candidate route for the animatic.

Author exactly five continuous shots as one motivated virtual-cinematography path, with narrative purpose, viewer takeaway, model action, camera, lighting, layout, transitions, rhythm, hold, copy, and truth constraints.

Base close-ups and component language on inspected GLB nodes and visible geometry; do not claim a verified production powertrain, manufacturing sequence, or engineering function that the concept asset does not establish.

Deliver deterministic camera state for every frame of the canonical 16-second, 30fps playback, including position, target, roll, FOV, focus distance, part state, light state, shot identity, and continuity metadata.

Translate the fixed-duration five-shot camera previs to one normalized reversible scroll timeline that visibly delivers virtual FPV infiltration, one occlusion-motivated hidden cut, cockpit deceleration, door breakout, restrained exterior arc, and a stable final hero hold.

Case research, route comparison, five-shot script, camera previs, and animatic remain mandatory inputs, but successful deterministic validation releases runtime implementation without a human screening or confirmation record.

The implemented page must use demand rendering, deterministic reverse scrolling, bounded roll, coordinated camera/parts/light/layout/copy, reduced-motion fallback, and measured desktop frame pacing; inspect the actual rendered delivery after implementation.

Before JavaScript, GLB decoding, texture upload, or shader compilation completes, the page must show a lightweight static poster aligned with the INTERCEPT composition; the first verified 3D product frame must replace it without an empty flash, and failure or reduced-motion routes must retain a meaningful product image.

Release acceptance requires a passing inspect-delivery-outcome record whose direct evidence covers actual browser pixels, deterministic replay, frame pacing, idle rendering, errors, and fallback behavior for the current runtime.
